title: session-start hook: detect .claude/commands/ out-of-sync with templates/commands/
summary: session-start.sh compares mtimes of templates/commands/wai-*.md vs .claude/commands/ counterparts. Any newer source file triggers a SYNC WARNING in the session init block.
why_bother: Skill sync gap caused 15-18k tokens/session waste for multiple sessions without detection. Keys skills were 370 lines behind the installed versions. The gap went undetected until manual discovery.
goal: SYNC WARNING appears in <wai-session-init> naming the specific out-of-sync files whenever templates/commands/ is ahead of .claude/commands/. No warning when in sync.
scope: session-start.sh: mtime comparison for all wai-*.md files across both dirs
Inject SYNC WARNING into <wai-session-init> CONTEXT HEALTH section if gap detected
Optional: add sync check to spoke_integrity_score.py (-2 points if gap > 0)
constraints: Only compare wai-*.md files (not teaching files, manifests, or other files in templates/commands/)
If .claude/commands/ file doesn't exist at all: that's also a sync warning
Warning must name the specific file(s), not just a count
No-op if all in sync — zero output impact
perceive: session-start.sh runs checks (historian, session guard, cc health) but does NOT compare templates/commands/ vs .claude/commands/. Currently in sync (diff shows 0 lines for wai.md, wai-closeout.md, wai-lug-schema.md). But .claude/commands/ has 2 extra files (wai-closeout-feedback-v2.md, wai-next.md) not in templates/commands/ — those are fine. templates/commands/ has manifest.json and a .teaching file not in .claude/commands/ — also fine. The risk is: any shipit delay causes the gap to silently reopen.
execute: 1. Read .claude/hooks/session-start.sh to find correct insertion point (after cc-advisor check, before outputting wai-session-init). 2. Add sync check bash block: iterate over templates/commands/wai-*.md; for each, check if corresponding .claude/commands/$(basename) exists and if templates version is newer (-nt test); collect out-of-sync names. 3. Build SYNC_WARNING string listing out-of-sync filenames. 4. In the wai-session-init CONTEXT HEALTH section output, add: if SYNC_WARNING non-empty: `SYNC: ⚠ out of sync: {files} — run /shipit`; if empty: `SYNC: OK`. 5. (Optional) In spoke_integrity_score.py: add a sync_gap check function that runs the same comparison and deducts 2 points from hooks dimension if gap found.
verify: Run: touch templates/commands/wai.md; bash .claude/hooks/session-start.sh 2>/dev/null | grep -i sync → should show 'SYNC: ⚠ out of sync: wai.md'. Then: touch .claude/commands/wai.md; bash .claude/hooks/session-start.sh | grep -i sync → 'SYNC: OK'.
acceptance_criteria: templates/commands/wai.md newer than .claude/commands/wai.md → SYNC WARNING appears naming wai.md
All wai-*.md files in sync → SYNC: OK in session init, no noise
.claude/commands/ missing a file that exists in templates/commands/ → named in warning
Warning text includes the specific filename(s), not just a count
session-start.sh exits 0 regardless of sync state (warning only, not blocking)
